editorial.headline: The Fisheries Support Code With a Bali Scope Test
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 03300 covers practical support around catching and aquaculture, nationally open to PMA, but Bali registration depends on the exact declared activity risk.
editorial.body:
KBLI 03300 is not the act of fishing itself, nor the later business of turning fish into a finished product. Its centre of gravity is the operational support that sits around capture and aquaculture: feeding services, harvesting assistance, auction preparation, sorting, grading, quality testing, and the handling needed before sale. The record also brings in preservation before the market, such as chilling fish to keep it fresh, along with fish protection, fisheries control or fish-guard work, and maritime ecosystem restoration.

That breadth matters. This is a service code for the infrastructure of fisheries activity, used by operators whose role is to make the catch or cultivation process workable, orderly, safer, or more market-ready before the product moves onward. It can fit small, practical service businesses as well as larger operators, because the record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. The scope is therefore not only a technical classification; it is a statement about where the business sits in the fisheries chain: close to production, before downstream distribution or processing, and tied to support rather than ownership of the fishery activity itself.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is clean. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a pma_max_asing of 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In ordinary language, that means the record treats the code as nationally open to foreign ownership up to 100%. There is no foreign-share cap below full ownership in the supplied data, so the editorial conclusion should not invent one. For founders comparing structures, the national rule is the easier part of the story: this code is open on the national investment list, and it is open across all stated business scales.

Bali is more exacting. The record does not mark the code as outright blocked in Bali, but it does assign Blocked (scope-dependent) and gives a clear warning: the OSS risk at Besar scale is low on some scopes and higher on others, so PMA registration in Bali is possible only by declaring the higher-risk scope and verifying live OSS against the exact activity. That sits against the province-wide moratorium rule blocking Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. The honest reading is therefore neither panic nor comfort: KBLI 03300 is nationally open, but in Bali a foreign-owned setup must be scoped with care, because the registration outcome turns on the declared activity rather than the title alone.
